thread:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT: Spike in model response contamination for model-family 'redwood-7b-v2' detected. Symptom: tokens from previous requests appearing in subsequent responses. Affected endpoints: hosted/redwood-7b-v2-prod-*, anomaly started=1912350900.

nina_oncall: I'm on it. Brief summary of impact? Any requests showing PII?

jess_support: We've got 3 customers reporting context bleed. Merchant-zen provided an example where order ids from customer A appeared in a reply to customer B. They claim no sensitive data but are panicked.

ryan_prod: Noted. Marking this P1 for customer-facing correctness. Eng-runtime + SRE please triage.

eng-runtime-bot: Correlating metrics... KV_cache_reuse_rate jumped after deploy 1912334000. seq_offset_mismatch_errors also increasing.

tom_runtime: grabbing runtime traces. Early look: the continuous batcher has been reusing KV slots across requests when sequence offsets don't align, and the guard that compares seq_offset was skipped under optimistic path. Example trace: ```
[12:34:45Z] req=xx1 model=redwood-7b-v2 seq_len=64 kv_slot=0x9f3a seq_offset=0 -> store
[12:34:46Z] req=yy2 model=redwood-7b-v2 seq_len=128 kv_slot=0x9f3a seq_offset=64 -> load returned old ctx
```

nina_oncall: That matches the client symptoms. What's the fastest mitigation we can do that doesn't require full rollback?

tom_runtime: Option A: globally turn off optimistic KV reuse for the family: `rbctl update feature --model-family redwood-7b-v2 --optimize_kv=false`. Option B: change continuous_batcher to enforce strict per-request kv validation: `rbctl update config --continuous-batcher.reuse_guard=strict`. Option C: emergency rollback of the last runtime image to the previous stable.

nina_oncall: Let's do A immediately (fast config flip) and B as a follow-up. Rollback only if impact doesn't drop.

eng-runtime-bot: Executing command: rbctl update feature --model-family redwood-7b-v2 --optimize_kv=false (requested by nina_oncall). Applying to edge pools now.

jess_support: Sent a short note to affected customers: "We've applied a mitigation that should eliminate cross-request context reuse. Please monitor and let us know if you continue to see anomalies."

tom_runtime: Kicking a targeted restart of runtimes handling that family: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/redwood-runtime --selector=family=redwood-7b-v2 --grace-period=30`. This picks up the config change without full cluster downtime.

eng-runtime-bot: Rollout in progress. Pods replaced sequentially.

nina_oncall: Watching metrics. How long until we expect visible change?

eng-runtime-bot: Metric window shows first pod replacements now. Past-1min sample: contamination_count per-minute dropping from 40 -> 9.

tom_runtime: After 6 pods replaced contamination rate down to 2/min. P95 latency unchanged. I still see a handful of nodes with old binary; scheduling system had them pinned by a daemonset; I'm removing the pin and draining them.

ryan_prod: Good. I'm drafting a customer update to say mitigation applied and RCA arriving in 48h. Keep me posted before sending.

jess_support: Customers acked receipt. Merchant-zen asked for an ETA for full fix. I told them we'll have a follow-up in ~24-48h with planned rollout.

nina_oncall: Next steps for engineering: 1) revert the optimistic reuse codepath or add seq_offset strict check, 2) add unit/integration tests for cross-request KV collisions (multi-tenant), 3) add anomaly alert (sensitivity to reuse metric) so we can auto-rollback in future. Tom, take point?

tom_runtime: Taking ownership. I'll open a PR to add a seq_offset invariant check: runtime should never return cached KV if seq_offset != expected. Also gating the feature behind a canary flag.

eng-runtime-bot: New incident ticket created: INC-2026-3152. Severity: Sev2. Owner: tom_runtime. Actions due: RCA + remediation plan within 48h.

nina_oncall: Handoff: Tom you own until 1912354850 for follow-up. If regressions reappear ping me. I'll monitor the post-mitigation window for two hours.

tom_runtime: Will add debug traces that include req_id, kv_slot, seq_offset when reuse occurs. Also plan: write a small repro script that simulates interleaved seq lengths to ensure no leakage.

jess_support: Uploading customer examples to the ticket now. Also requesting consent logs to verify no PII leaked; I'll escalate if anything sensitive appears.

nina_oncall: Thanks all. Current status: mitigation applied, contamination count down to near-zero, customers notified, owner assigned. End of active handoff. :white_check_mark:
